body_markdown:
Five dividend-paying[AI infrastructure stocks](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/five-dividend-paying-ai-tech-stocks-to-buy/) to buy are favored by market forecasters that include BofA Global Research.


Bullish positioning and fears of an eventual slowdown in hyperscaler capex spending are among the reasons why now may be a good time to view the selloff in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure stocks as a buying opportunity, according to BofA Global Research. The investment firm’s July Fund Manager Survey indicated that “long global semiconductors” were viewed as the most crowded trade.


Though consensus analysts’ forecasts do not expect annual capital expenditure (capex) growth across five major U.S. cloud vendors to peak in 2026, growth rates in 2027 are expected to remain strong at 39%, BofA wrote in an Aug. 14 research note. Plus, 12 months of upward revisions could be in store to current capex estimates, it added.


With positive earnings-per-share (EPS) revisions continuing for many AI stocks, with individual price-to-earnings (P/E) valuations compressing to levels well below the S&P average in many cases, despite substantial growth ahead for 2027, BofA analysts identified their preferred picks from the AI stocks caught in the selloff.


Bryan Perry, a seasoned Wall Street denizen who heads the[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) investment newsletter and the[Breakout Blue Chip Trader](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/breakout-blue-chip-trader-web-default/?source=GURUBBCT1) advisory service, voiced optimism about the markets. Stocks were supported Wednesday, Aug. 19, by some easing in longer-term yields after the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced it will at least double the size of liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated nominal coupon securities, he wrote in the Aug. 20 edition of his[Hi-Tech Trader](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/htt-default/?source=GURUHTT1) advisory service. The move pushed yields lower and precious metals higher, he added.


*Bryan Perry heads the[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) investment newsletter.*


**Five Dividend-paying AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy, BofA Says: LRCX**


Fremont, California-based Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ:[LRCX](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lam-research-announces-plans-to-invest-more-than-3b-to-expand-global-lab-network-increase-innovation-velocity-in-the-ai-era-302851309.html#financial-modal) ) announced big plans on Aug. 23 to invest more than $3 billion during the next five years to expand its global research and development (R&D) lab network. The planned multi-site expansion is expected to add infrastructure and capabilities to increase experiment capacity by more than 50%, the company announced.


As an AI infrastructure company, Lam’s R&D approach combines specialized labs worldwide, each built to accelerate a distinct step of the innovation cycle, with customer collaboration that includes locations near customer facilities, company officials said. Lam aims for its labs to operate as an integrated 24/7 network, enabling innovation in parallel and at scale, according to its announcement.


With the investment, Lam intends to further compress product development cycles for customers, from pathfinding to fab deployment. Lam’s global lab network spans the United States, Asia and Europe with combined R&D infrastructure supporting more than one million experiments annually, its officials reported. Facilities specialized for foundational research in new chemistries, materials and mechatronics have the capability to compress weeks of experimental work into as little as a few days in some cases.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


One market tracker who has recommended Lam Research in the past is Jim Woods, who heads the *[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS)* investment newsletter and the[TNT Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tnt-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUTNT) ,[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) *,*[Five Star Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/five-star-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUFST) and[Bullseye Stock Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/bullseye-default/?source=GURUBEST1) advisory services that recommend both stocks and options. Woods is watching AI infrastructure stocks closely and sees opportunity.


*Paul Dykewicz meets with Jim Woods, who heads[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS) .*


BofA wrote that even though Lam Research shares have performed well year to date, the investment firm expects to outperform as it keeps gain share and expands margins inside a “powerful” multi-year wafer fab equipment (WFE) cycle.


**Five Dividend-paying AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy, BofA Says: ORCL**


Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) shares are down roughly 30% since June as investors have grown increasingly concerned about AI-related return on invested capital (ROIC) and near-term profitability, leaving the stock trading at a relatively low 16x calendar year 2027 estimated price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, BofA wrote in a recent research note. However, recent results from hyperscalers, including Microsoft and Amazon, have further demonstrated that AI infrastructure investments can drive meaningful revenue growth and profitability, reinforcing the conviction that Oracle’s current spending cycle is creating long-term value.


“We believe the stock’s recent pullback creates an attractive entry point, particularly as Oracle’s remaining performance obligations (RPO) have grown to a whopping $638 billion,” BofA wrote. That provides strong revenue visibility over the next few years, it added.


“While the company faces significant capital requirements to support this buildout, we view management’s disciplined approach to balancing debt and equity financing as a prudent strategy that positions Oracle to capitalize on the AI opportunity while maintaining financial flexibility,” BofA continued.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Five Dividend-paying AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy, BofA Says: VRT**


Westerville, Ohio-based Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE: VRT) is a designer, builder and provider of critical digital infrastructure services that offers a modest dividend yield of 0.085%. The company also provides core power management, thermal liquid cooling, racks and monitoring software for data centers, communication networks and industrial facilities.


Dr. Robert Castellano, PhD, a senior analyst with[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU) and several advisory services led by technology futurist George Gilder, told me that he thinks Vertiv has been “beaten down too much.” Vertiv supplies the power and cooling equipment needed inside AI data centers, and there is no AI buildout without either one, said Dr. Castellano, who also heads the[Information Network](https://www.theinformationnet.com/about-us) consultancy.


*George Gilder heads[Gilder’s Moonshots](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-moonshots-launch/?source=GURUMS01) .*


Vertiv’s second-quarter sales increased 24%, adjusted earnings soared 60% and its management raised its guidance for 2026, Castellano said. That does not look like a company whose business is weakening, added Dr. Castellano, who also works on advisory services such as[Gilder’s Moonshots](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-moonshots-launch/?source=GURUMS01) ,[Gilder’s Private Reserve](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/private-default/?source=GURUGPR1) and[Gilder’s Tech Income Accelerator](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilder-tech-report-pro-launch/?source=GTRPROGURU) .


“The stock is volatile, but AI racks keep using more power and generating more heat, which increases the amount of Vertiv equipment needed in each data center,” Dr. Castellano told me. “I see the pullback as a buying opportunity.”


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Five Dividend-paying AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy, BofA Says: MU**


Boise, Idaho-based Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU), announced Aug. 13 that it would launch the Micron Ventures Paradigm Fund, a $250 million investment vehicle built to partner with the companies shaping the future of AI. Micron Ventures’ third and largest fund to date, the Paradigm Fund, will invest across the full AI technology stack, from model architectures and compute infrastructure to enterprise applications and physical AI, the company announced.


As AI advances from generative models to systems that can reason, act and interact with the physical world, the demands on compute, memory and storage change, the company continued. The Paradigm Fund is structured to give Micron deeper partnerships with the innovators shaping these shifts and earlier insight into the technologies that will define the future of AI infrastructure.


“We’re in an exciting era of paradigm shifts, each one redefining what AI can do and what it requires,” said Rene Hartner, vice president of corporate development at Micron, in a prepared statement. “These advancements converge on one common need: high-performance memory and storage solutions. Micron’s Paradigm Fund will invest in and partner with startups driving these innovations and strengthen our ability to deliver leading memory and storage solutions to meet the growing AI demands.”


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**BofA’s Analysis**


Micron shares are about 34% below their 52-week high as investors position ahead of an eventual memory downturn, but BofA countered that it views the reset as an “enhanced buying opportunity,” given the stock already discounts a severe cyclical outcome while assigning little to no value to MU’s High Bandwidth Memory (HBM)/AI businesses or improved earnings-per-share (EPS) sustainability. HBM is valuable as a provider of fast computer memory used in graphics cards and AI processors.


AI is broadening memory demand beyond HBM as larger model weights and longer context windows increase requirements for weights and Key-Value (KV) cache, while open-model deployments create incremental memory sockets across HBM, dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and enterprise NAND. KV cache is a memory optimization technique used in Large Language Models (LLMs) and Transformer architectures to speed up text generation, while NAND flash memory is a type of chip storage used in solid-state drives (SSDs), phones and USB drives.


BoA rates MU as a buy and predicts that supply constraints support durable memory pricing.


Jim Woods recommended Micron earlier in the year in a trading service and led his subscribes to profits in the stock and the related options. He currently is recommending technology giant Apple, Inc. (AAPL), of Cupertino, California, in the Growth Accelerators Portfolio of his[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS) investment newsletter. Woods wrote that he expects to own the dividend-paying stock for years to come.


**Five Dividend-paying AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy, BofA Says: STX**


Seagate Technology Holdings PLC (NASDAQ: STX), legally incorporated in Dublin, Ireland, with its principal executive offices located in Singapore and a significant operational headquarters in Fremont, California, is another AI infrastructure buy recommendation. Bargain hunters may like that it fell 9.63% on Tuesday, Aug. 18.


The company is a global data storage company founded in 1978 that designs, develops and manufactures electronic data storage products, specializing primarily in hard disk drives (HDDs) and mass-capacity storage solutions for enterprise data centers, cloud systems and consumer markets. Certain market followers indicated that Seagate fell due to a combination of profit-taking after a multi-month rally and a broader tech-sector pullback that affected AI-linked hardware stocks.


BofA has a buy recommendation on Seagate and a price target of $1,150 per share. After years of being plagued by oversupply, the Hard Disk Drive (HDD) industry is now structurally better with the three vendors, Seagate, Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC) and privately held Toshiba, maintaining discipline on supply addition and limiting bit growth to be driven by density improvement. On this path, Seagate enjoys a lead with its HAMR (Heat Assisted Magnetic Recording) technology that has been adopted by major hyperscale customers, BofA wrote.


Furthermore, visibility continues to improve with build-to-order (BTO) contracts through the end of FY27, while vast majority of the company’s nearline exabytes (EB) being allocation into calendar 2028, and customers are extending planning horizons into calendar year 2029 and beyond, BofA continued. The investment firm forecast Seagate would benefit from secular demand from cloud, continued strong pricing and margin improvement.

**Geopolitics**


With military action taking place in multiple places in the world, particularly in Iran and between Russia and Ukraine, geopolitical risk remains a big concern. These three investments offer a potentially profitable way to achieve share-price appreciation amid the chaos.


Investors willing to trade options also may want to try an advisory service that teaches them how to do so. As long as there is turmoil in the world… wars, tariffs, political upheaval, you name it, “we make money,” said Grossman.


“We can’t control the events of the day, but we can take advantage of that instability by trading short-term movements,” Grossman commented. “Options on SPY provide outstanding leverage and liquidity for quick profits.”
